title: Analog Cosmology in a Quenched Bose-Einstein Condensate Bubble
authors: Ruotong Zhai, Brendan Rhyno, Zain Mehdi, Naceur Gaaloul, Smitha Vishveshwara, Daniel E. Sheehy
abstract: Recent interest and realization of ultracold bosons confined in shell-shaped, or bubble, traps have opened up several directions in the study of Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) in intrinsically curved geometries. Here, we explore the prospect of using thin spherical shell-shaped BECs as analog gravity simulators of an expanding or contracting curved universe. We study an interacting BEC bubble subject to a temporal quench of the interaction strength. Our theoretical approach, which uses a Bogoliubov treatment following a dimensional reduction of a spherical BEC to the low-energy excitations of a shell-shaped structure, demonstrates how this system serves as a laboratory analog for a positively curved universe having a time-varying scale factor. We investigate spontaneous pair production triggered by quenches associated with exponentially decaying or growing interaction strengths, focusing on the emergence of oscillations in the structure factor---analogous to Sakharov oscillations in the Cosmic Microwave Background angular power spectrum. We quantify the entanglement of the produced pairs via logarithmic negativity, and show how this measure may be extracted from the power spectrum. These findings establish a bridge between quantum information science and early-universe cosmology in a laboratory setting.
summary: This paper demonstrates that Bose-Einstein Condensates confined to spherical shells can act as analog simulators for curved spacetime cosmology. By quenching the interaction strength, the system exhibits quantum particle production analogous to processes in the early universe, allowing entanglement to be quantified using measurable spectral features.
main_problem: The study explores using thin spherical shell-shaped Bose-Einstein Condensates (BECs) as analog gravity simulators to model the dynamics of an expanding or contracting curved universe.
main_result: The system successfully models a positively curved universe with a time-varying scale factor, demonstrating spontaneous pair production characterized by oscillations analogous to Sakharov oscillations in the CMB.
method: The theoretical approach involves dimensional reduction to an effective 2D Hamiltonian, followed by a Bogoliubov treatment to analyze quantum fluctuations.
model_or_system: The physical system is an interacting BEC confined to a spherical shell. The dynamics are modeled by an effective 2D Hamiltonian, which is analyzed by linearizing the equations of motion for density and phase fluctuations.
key_observables: Spontaneous pair production, the structure factor S_l(t) (analogous to CMB power spectrum), and the logarithmic negativity (measure of entanglement).
important_parameters: Time-varying interaction strength (quench protocol), effective wavevector k, and the shell geometry parameters (radius R, thickness $\Delta R$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the thin-shell limit (dimensional reduction) and the Bogoliubov approximation for fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate quantum particle production from both increasing and decreasing coupling quenches, showing the time-dependent structure factor and density-density correlation function.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical analogy using the 3D Hamiltonian to deriving the effective 2D Hamiltonian. It then solves the linearized equations of motion across multiple quench regimes, finally calculating observables like entanglement and particle production amplitudes.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable laboratory platform (BECs) to simulate fundamental cosmological processes like inflation and particle creation, bridging quantum information theory and early-universe cosmology.
